clue.text: In a sorry state after crashing Citroen, entering junction

indicators.note: the junction letter goes into the middle of the scrambled car name
a car crashing ends up mangled, so the letters of the car name are rearranged

parts.note: T is a T-junction, a road junction shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A motorist is in a sorry state after writing off their Citroen at a junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' turns CITROEN into CONTRIE; 'entering' puts T inside it, after CONTRI. 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contrite is penitent, full of remorse, which is being in a sorry state.

clue.text: Actors willing to start knitting

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
'I'm on' means I'm willing, game for it

explanation.surface: Performers keen to take up knitting between scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast on is to put the first row of stitches on the needle, beginning a piece of knitting.

clue.text: Name these girls cruelly, to incense

indicators.note: treated cruelly, the word incense is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling these girls names cruelly, just to make them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: N (Name) plus the answer, rearranged ('cruelly'), make INCENSE; so INCENSE minus N, rearranged, gives the girls. 'these' points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nieces are the daughters of one's siblings, so they are girls in the family.

clue.text: Enter into custody following fracas

indicators.note: a fracas is a noisy brawl, so the letters of the two words get knocked about

explanation.surface: A suspect is taken into custody after a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracas' rearranges ENTER INTO; 'following' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is holding on to something or someone, as custody keeps a person detained.

clue.text: Rolls in a row — indicative of poverty

definitions.meaning: read literally, bread rolls lined up form a line of bread
being 'on' this phrase means living at subsistence level, barely able to afford food

explanation.surface: Rolls lined up in a queue, a sign of poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from queues for free bread, so being on it signals hardship; literally, rolls in a line.

clue.text: Southern pride damaged by Bruce's inspiration?

indicators.note: damaged pride is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish king's pride was hurt, but something gave him the will to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce, a Scottish king, is said to have watched a spider keep trying to spin its web and taken heart to fight on.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says a persistent web-spinner, seen in a cave, inspired Robert the Bruce to persevere.

clue.text: Fish — or the rest of the bird?

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish with a spiny fin
a bird rests on a branch or rod, its roost

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a fish or where a bird rests.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a freshwater fish and also a bird's roosting place.

clue.text: Fruity role for Shakespearian comic

parts.note: the clown constable in Much Ado About Nothing has a name that is also a wild fruit, so the role is fruity

explanation.surface: A juicy part for a comic actor in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' looks like a judgement on the role's richness; it means the character's name is the name of a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bumbling constable in Much Ado About Nothing shares his name with the fruit of the dogwood.

clue.text: Have second thoughts about steamer crossing stormy seas

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: a steamer crossing the seas sits in the middle of them
stormy seas are churned up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Doubts creep in for someone on a steamer heading into stormy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' turns SEAS into AESS; 'crossing' puts SS inside, giving ASSESS, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To think again about a decision is to reconsider it, having second thoughts.

clue.text: Haggard female playing with death — just in case

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, named after its immortal heroine

indicators.note: playing with the word death means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A gaunt woman toys with death, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like gaunt, but it is the author H. Rider Haggard, whose famous novel is called She.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword put back in its scabbard is kept in a case, so the definition is literal.

clue.text: Grab me — fracturing part of skull

indicators.note: fracturing breaks the two words apart, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed fractures a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists name the point on the top of the skull where two sutures meet with this term.

clue.text: One type of soup received glumly — I want a different variety

indicators.note: a different variety of the words is the same letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner receives a soup glumly and asks for another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different variety' rearranges GLUMLY I WANT A; 'received' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a curried soup from Anglo-Indian cooking, its name from Tamil for pepper water.

clue.text: Party rejected one trip to theatre

indicators.note: rejected sends the party back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: a trip upsets the word one, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A partygoer turns down an outing to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DO into OD; 'trip' rearranges ONE into EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a chain of cinemas, and the word was a Greek building for music, a kind of theatre.

clue.text: In such turbulent conditions, shag and duck sure to take a battering

indicators.note: words that take a battering are knocked about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A cormorant and a duck are buffeted in a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A shag is a seabird, a kind of cormorant, which suits the stormy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy waves on open water make for turbulent conditions at sea.

clue.text: Claim rescuer somehow achieves amazing recoveries

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters come together in some unexpected order

explanation.surface: A rescuer claims to bring about astonishing recoveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden healings that defy medicine are thought of as wondrous recoveries.

clue.text: Money for a beer? Nothing in it — try here!

definitions.text: Money for a beer? Nothing in it — try here!

parts.note: cash is ready money

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the beer just named

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, the usual order
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with no money for a drink is told where to get some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts O inside PINT, giving POINT; 'for' is only a link. The whole clue also points to a machine that dispenses money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine is where you would go to get money when your wallet is empty.

clue.text: This optical device cunningly copies first page to the last

indicators.note: cunningly suggests the word copies is cleverly reworked, its letters rearranged
the first letter of the word page is taken
the last letter of the word the is taken

explanation.surface: An optical device that cleverly copies a page from first to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' rearranges COPIES into EPISCO; 'first' takes P from page and 'last' takes E from the; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a projector that throws an image of an opaque object such as a page onto a screen.

clue.text: Angry exchanges with war article missing some points of view

indicators.note: missing means the word war lacks the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
an angle is a point of view, a way of looking at something

explanation.surface: Heated rows over a war, missing some viewpoints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes A out of WAR, leaving WR; 'with' and 'some' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Long, bad-tempered arguments are quarrels, which is what angry exchanges are.

clue.text: A bump on the head should attract his attention

definitions.text: A bump on the head should attract his attention

parts.words: A bump on the head should attract his attention
parts.note: not an injury: practitioners of a Victorian pseudoscience read character from the bumps of the skull

explanation.surface: A head injury that someone ought to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a doctor tending a knock on the head; the man in question reads skull contours to judge personality.
explanation.definitionFit: These Victorian practitioners claimed bumps on the skull revealed mental faculties.

clue.text: A wild shot at parking — such language follows!

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: a wild shot goes astray, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver misses a parking space and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SHOT into SHTO; 'at' is a link. 'such language follows' jokes that bad language comes after a botched parking attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is a language of Afghanistan and Pakistan, spoken by the Pashtuns.

clue.text: Any huge characters won't quite fit into this bush but

indicators.note: characters here are letters, jumbled together in a new order
not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Anyone huge would struggle to squeeze into this little shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't quite' cuts HUGE to HUG; 'characters' rearranges ANY + HUG. The page prints 'but', an OCR misread of 'hut'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian Aboriginal shelter of bark and branches is a simple hut in the bush.

clue.text: Worn by nun, on best outing?

definitions.text: Worn by nun, on best outing?

indicators.note: an outing takes the words out and about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat a nun might wear on her best trip out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' rearranges NUN ON BEST; the whole clue also describes the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed bonnet shielding the face from the sun is headwear for an outdoor trip.

clue.text: Different route to the exterior

indicators.note: a different route takes the same letters in another order

explanation.surface: Taking another road out to the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer describes the side away from the centre, the exterior.

clue.text: Universal type of seal overturned this Malay boat

indicators.note: in a down-and-across sense, overturned means the letters run in the opposite order

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
the harp seal is a species of seal

explanation.surface: A seal capsizes a small boat in Malay waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses U + HARP, giving the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A prahu is a fast Malay sailing craft, often with an outrigger.

clue.text: Rock where two ducks perch, reportedly

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, O, so two give two of them

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it sounds rather than as it is written

parts.note: to light is to settle or perch, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A rock where a pair of ducks is said to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns LIGHT into a soundalike spelling; 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolite is a limestone made of tiny rounded grains like fish roe.

clue.text: How sly two eyes, it's said, might appear, blinking in this fashion?

indicators.note: it's said means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the words run together with two I sounds, the two eyes, to sound like the answer's syllables

explanation.surface: Someone with a pair of sly eyes blinks knowingly.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'how' plus 'I' plus 'sly' with the eyes as I sounds approximates the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl blinks slowly with wide eyes, so blinking like one is doing it in a wise-bird manner.

clue.text: Don't quite denounce warrant

indicators.note: not quite the full word, so a letter is left off its front

parts.note: to censure is to denounce or condemn

explanation.surface: An instruction not quite to condemn a warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't quite' cuts the first letter from CENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to guarantee it, make it certain.

clue.text: See, also, the docked canine

parts.note: to eye is to see, look at
too means also

indicators.note: docked means cut short, like a tail, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Look, a dog with a docked tail too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts THE to TH. 'canine' looks like dog, but it is the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tooth below the eye is called the canine.
